    "text": "## 7. Agent-Facing Contract",
    "sectionText": "## 7. Agent-Facing Contract\n\nThe current door is `fgos dispatch recover <runId>`, without `--action` for\nread-only observation. It builds a snapshot of the Run, visibility, outbox,\ncontroller evidence, real control epoch and settled signal, then returns a\nrecommendation, `needs-input` or `park`. The intent is `resume` or `reassign`;\nthe default is defined by the CLI/use case, not by a coordination-session scan.\n\nResume requires explicit non-fresh driver-liveness evidence; fresh or unknown\nfreshness parks. Reassignment requires replacement-authority evidence naming a\ndriver, read from controller-owned state, never worker-writable outbox claims.\nUnknown evidence parks; a settled Run has nothing to recover. A recommendation\ncontains `snapshotHash`, `expectedControlEpoch`, `actionKey`, `evidenceIds`,\n`action`, `expiresAt` and `reason`; the default lifetime is five minutes.\n\nApply uses the same door with `--action`, `--expected-snapshot`,\n`--expected-control-epoch`, `--expected-expires-at` and `--action-key`.\nIt re-reads facts, checks action-key binding, snapshot, epoch, expiry and\npresent legality, then acquires real Run control and checks settlement again.\nStale/expired plans, missing authority and held live control are refused or\nparked rather than overridden. Repeating a consumed action key returns the\nrecorded `already-applied` outcome.\n\nSuccessful apply records the recovery command, updates the control-epoch\nprojection and attempts the applicable dispatch-claim clear. It does not itself\nlaunch a replacement worker, close a session or advance a Workflow. Dormant\nsession-ownership checks still refuse `resume-driver` for old session-owned\nAssignments; this is not a claim that the retired coordination door exists.\n\nImplementation evidence: `src/runner/dispatch/recovery-planner.mjs:118-173,\n243-316,319-361` and `src/verbs/dispatch/recover.mjs:95-132,266-408`.\nRead the [area portal](../README.md) and [runner spec](../../../specs/runner.md)\nfor the wider execution boundary; recovery here does not own Work lifecycle."
  },

        "text": "## 7. Agent-Facing Contract",
        "sectionText": "## 7. Agent-Facing Contract\n\nExtend the existing `coordination run` request door with a proposed recovery\nrequest variant: `{contract, coordinationId, writerId, intent: recover,\ntarget?: {assignmentId}, budgetGrantRef?: string}`. Omitted target scans the\nsession; engine chooses one eligible action and returns progress. `show --json`\nexposes the same typed recommendation without refreshing/writing runtime facts.\nThe headless adapter calls the same use case. These are proposed request fields,\nnot commands/features available in the current release. A fresh controller may\nomit `writerId` only when the session manifest supplies a replacement-driver\ngrant; otherwise the request returns `needs-input` with the exact identity\nrequirement. Recovery executes exactly the planner's selected action. It does\nnot unconditionally call close-after-steps; close is invoked only when the\nselected action is `close-session`.\n\nReturn `{outcome: applied | already-applied | waiting | needs-input | refused,\naction, subjectRefs, reasonCode, evidenceRefs, nextCheckAt?}`. A repeated recover\ncall recomputes facts and resumes a durable pending action. It never uses a\nworker-supplied child ID, task key, supersession boolean or ownership assertion.\n`needs-input` names the exact missing semantic decision/grant; it is not the\ndefault for ordinary concurrency, a slow observer or already-applied action.\nBlocked targets remain individually visible; another eligible independent target\nmay progress. Stable ordering prevents one parked target monopolizing the scan."
      }
    },

      "text": "## 7. Agent-Facing Contract",
      "sectionText": "## 7. Agent-Facing Contract\n\nExtend the existing `coordination run` request door with a proposed recovery\nrequest variant: `{contract, coordinationId, writerId, intent: recover,\ntarget?: {assignmentId}, budgetGrantRef?: string}`. Omitted target scans the\nsession; engine chooses one eligible action and returns progress. `show --json`\nexposes the same typed recommendation without refreshing/writing runtime facts.\nThe headless adapter calls the same use case. These are proposed request fields,\nnot commands/features available in the current release. A fresh controller may\nomit `writerId` only when the session manifest supplies a replacement-driver\ngrant; otherwise the request returns `needs-input` with the exact identity\nrequirement. Recovery executes exactly the planner's selected action. It does\nnot unconditionally call close-after-steps; close is invoked only when the\nselected action is `close-session`.\n\nReturn `{outcome: applied | already-applied | waiting | needs-input | refused,\naction, subjectRefs, reasonCode, evidenceRefs, nextCheckAt?}`. A repeated recover\ncall recomputes facts and resumes a durable pending action. It never uses a\nworker-supplied child ID, task key, supersession boolean or ownership assertion.\n`needs-input` names the exact missing semantic decision/grant; it is not the\ndefault for ordinary concurrency, a slow observer or already-applied action.\nBlocked targets remain individually visible; another eligible independent target\nmay progress. Stable ordering prevents one parked target monopolizing the scan."
    }
  },

    "text": "## 7. Agent-Facing Contract",
    "sectionText": "## 7. Agent-Facing Contract\n\nThe current door is `fgos dispatch recover <runId>`, without `--action` for\nread-only observation. It builds a snapshot of the Run, visibility, outbox,\ncontroller evidence, real control epoch and settled signal, then returns a\nrecommendation, `needs-input` or `park`. The intent is `resume` or `reassign`;\nthe default is defined by the CLI/use case, not by a coordination-session scan.\n\nResume requires explicit non-fresh driver-liveness evidence; fresh or unknown\nfreshness parks. Reassignment requires replacement-authority evidence naming a\ndriver, read from controller-owned state, never worker-writable outbox claims.\nUnknown evidence parks; a settled Run has nothing to recover. A recommendation\ncontains `snapshotHash`, `expectedControlEpoch`, `actionKey`, `evidenceIds`,\n`action`, `expiresAt` and `reason`; the default lifetime is five minutes.\n\nApply uses the same door with `--action`, `--expected-snapshot`,\n`--expected-control-epoch`, `--expected-expires-at` and `--action-key`.\nIt re-reads facts, checks action-key binding, snapshot, epoch, expiry and\npresent legality, then acquires real Run control and checks settlement again.\nStale/expired plans, missing authority and held live control are refused or\nparked rather than overridden. Repeating a consumed action key returns the\nrecorded `already-applied` outcome.\n\nSuccessful apply records the recovery command, updates the control-epoch\nprojection and attempts the applicable dispatch-claim clear. It does not itself\nlaunch a replacement worker, close a session or advance a Workflow. Dormant\nsession-ownership checks still refuse `resume-driver` for old session-owned\nAssignments; this is not a claim that the retired coordination door exists.\n\nImplementation evidence: `src/runner/dispatch/recovery-planner.mjs:118-173,\n243-316,319-361` and `src/verbs/dispatch/recover.mjs:95-132,266-408`.\nRead the [area portal](../README.md) and [runner spec](../../../specs/runner.md)\nfor the wider execution boundary; recovery here does not own Work lifecycle."
  },

    "text": "## 7. Agent-Facing Contract",
    "sectionText": "## 7. Agent-Facing Contract\n\nThe current door is `fgos dispatch recover <runId>`, without `--action` for\nread-only observation. It builds a snapshot of the Run, visibility, outbox,\ncontroller evidence, real control epoch and settled signal, then returns a\nrecommendation, `needs-input` or `park`. The intent is `resume` or `reassign`;\nthe default is defined by the CLI/use case, not by a coordination-session scan.\n\nResume requires explicit non-fresh driver-liveness evidence; fresh or unknown\nfreshness parks. Reassignment requires replacement-authority evidence naming a\ndriver, read from controller-owned state, never worker-writable outbox claims.\nUnknown evidence parks; a settled Run has nothing to recover. A recommendation\ncontains `snapshotHash`, `expectedControlEpoch`, `actionKey`, `evidenceIds`,\n`action`, `expiresAt` and `reason`; the default lifetime is five minutes.\n\nApply uses the same door with `--action`, `--expected-snapshot`,\n`--expected-control-epoch`, `--expected-expires-at` and `--action-key`.\nIt re-reads facts, checks action-key binding, snapshot, epoch, expiry and\npresent legality, then acquires real Run control and checks settlement again.\nStale/expired plans, missing authority and held live control are refused or\nparked rather than overridden. Repeating a consumed action key returns the\nrecorded `already-applied` outcome.\n\nSuccessful apply records the recovery command, updates the control-epoch\nprojection and attempts the applicable dispatch-claim clear. It does not itself\nlaunch a replacement worker, close a session or advance a Workflow. Dormant\nsession-ownership checks still refuse `resume-driver` for old session-owned\nAssignments; this is not a claim that the retired coordination door exists.\n\nImplementation evidence: `src/runner/dispatch/recovery-planner.mjs:118-173,\n243-316,319-361` and `src/verbs/dispatch/recover.mjs:95-132,266-408`.\nRead the [area portal](../README.md) and [runner spec](../../../specs/runner.md)\nfor the wider execution boundary; recovery here does not own Work lifecycle."
  },

      "text": "## 7. Agent-Facing Contract",
      "sectionText": "## 7. Agent-Facing Contract\n\nThe current door is `fgos dispatch recover <runId>`, without `--action` for\nread-only observation. It builds a snapshot of the Run, visibility, outbox,\ncontroller evidence, real control epoch and settled signal, then returns a\nrecommendation, `needs-input` or `park`. The intent is `resume` or `reassign`;\nthe default is defined by the CLI/use case, not by a coordination-session scan.\n\nResume requires explicit non-fresh driver-liveness evidence; fresh or unknown\nfreshness parks. Reassignment requires replacement-authority evidence naming a\ndriver, read from controller-owned state, never worker-writable outbox claims.\nUnknown evidence parks; a settled Run has nothing to recover. A recommendation\ncontains `snapshotHash`, `expectedControlEpoch`, `actionKey`, `evidenceIds`,\n`action`, `expiresAt` and `reason`; the default lifetime is five minutes.\n\nApply uses the same door with `--action`, `--expected-snapshot`,\n`--expected-control-epoch`, `--expected-expires-at` and `--action-key`.\nIt re-reads facts, checks action-key binding, snapshot, epoch, expiry and\npresent legality, then acquires real Run control and checks settlement again.\nStale/expired plans, missing authority and held live control are refused or\nparked rather than overridden. Repeating a consumed action key returns the\nrecorded `already-applied` outcome.\n\nSuccessful apply records the recovery command, updates the control-epoch\nprojection and attempts the applicable dispatch-claim clear. It does not itself\nlaunch a replacement worker, close a session or advance a Workflow. Dormant\nsession-ownership checks still refuse `resume-driver` for old session-owned\nAssignments; this is not a claim that the retired coordination door exists.\n\nImplementation evidence: `src/runner/dispatch/recovery-planner.mjs:118-173,\n243-316,319-361` and `src/verbs/dispatch/recover.mjs:95-132,266-408`.\nRead the [area portal](../README.md) and [runner spec](../../runner/README.md)\nfor the wider execution boundary; recovery here does not own Work lifecycle."
    },

The\n  first useful proof fixture is a Master Coordination style loop with external\n  driver authority, bounded optional rounds, recheck, and disposition.\n- [Step 10: Coding Domain Adoption Of The Coordination Foundation](../../proposals/step-10-coding-domain-adoption.md)\n  discusses bringing the existing coding domain onto the Step 08 foundation:\n  duplicate-mechanism inventory, seams, the foundation capabilities coding\n  still needs, and a candidate step sequence gated on ADR-010 §5's proof.\n- [Component Authority Boundary Map](../../proposals/component-authority-boundary-map.md)\n  is the parallel architect-level authority/layout draft for cross-component\n  placement and forbidden dependencies."

    "text": "#### 9. Physical Placement",
    "sectionText": "#### 9. Physical Placement\n\nThe public command name stays `fgos` — runtime identity is the release digest, not the name, and every skill, hook, plugin, and Herdr call already targets `fgos <verb>`. `fgctl` is a separate bootstrap binary, not a renamed `fgos`. Crate names are kebab-case with an `fgos-` prefix; modules are snake_case.\n\n\nAdded in candidate: this retained source detail is carried verbatim in [the dropped-004 restoration](architecture/release-boundaries.md#restored-physical-placement-layout-tree).\n\n\nR1 is three crates: `fgos`, `fgos-host-runtime`, `fgos-distribution`. The legacy exec lane is a module inside `apps/fgos`, not a crate, because it is CLI-adapter-local (§4). `component-protocol` waits for R2 (only an external-process adapter needs `EncodedMessage`). Extract further crates only when pressure is real. Neither app owns provider selection; neither host use case imports another; every host feeds the shared authority/router/contracts layer, and provider adapters depend on component protocols, not host presentation. A component is not created merely because one proof verb is convenient (`gate-bypass` stays under its settled authority, not a manufactured `gate-policy` component).\n\nDistribution selects and activates the trusted runtime (`fgctl`: acquire/stage/verify/activate/upgrade/rollback); host invocation routes inside the activated runtime. Packaging-distribution owns the onboarding command vocabulary: local `fgos init` adopts a workspace under the active identity on first use, `fgos doctor --fix` performs every later registered repair, and the target architecture has no separate `setup` verb. See [Runtime Identity And Activation](../../architect/packaging-distribution/runtime-identity-and-activation.md)."

Crate names are kebab-case with an `fgos-` prefix; modules are snake_case.\n\n\nAdded in candidate: this retained source detail is carried verbatim in [the dropped-004 restoration](architecture/release-boundaries.md#restored-physical-placement-layout-tree).\n\n\nR1 is three crates: `fgos`, `fgos-host-runtime`, `fgos-distribution`. The legacy exec lane is a module inside `apps/fgos`, not a crate, because it is CLI-adapter-local (§4). `component-protocol` waits for R2 (only an external-process adapter needs `EncodedMessage`). Extract further crates only when pressure is real. Neither app owns provider selection; neither host use case imports another; every host feeds the shared authority/router/contracts layer, and provider adapters depend on component protocols, not host presentation. A component is not created merely because one proof verb is convenient (`gate-bypass` stays under its settled authority, not a manufactured `gate-policy` component).\n\nDistribution selects and activates the trusted runtime (`fgctl`: acquire/stage/verify/activate/upgrade/rollback); host invocation routes inside the activated runtime. Packaging-distribution owns the onboarding command vocabulary: local `fgos init` adopts a workspace under the active identity on first use, `fgos doctor --fix` performs every later registered repair, and the target architecture has no separate `setup` verb. See [Runtime Identity And Activation](../packaging-distribution/architecture/runtime-identity-and-activation.md)."
  },

        "text": "## 9. Physical Placement",
        "sectionText": "## 9. Physical Placement\n\nThe public command name stays `fgos` — runtime identity is the release digest, not the name, and every skill, hook, plugin, and Herdr call already targets `fgos <verb>`. `fgctl` is a separate bootstrap binary, not a renamed `fgos`. Crate names are kebab-case with an `fgos-` prefix; modules are snake_case.\n\n```txt\nCargo.toml                           # workspace root; herdr-plugin/ excluded in R1\napps/\n  fgos/                              # crate `fgos`, binary `fgos` — thin CLI adapter\n    src/cli_projector.rs             # argv -> OperationRequest\n    src/cli_presenter.rs             # ProviderOutcome -> fgos.v1 / exit code\n    src/legacy_exec.rs               # CommandRouteDescriptor lookup + Node payload exec\n  gateway/                           # later: thin REST/MCP/remote adapter (repo-layout-vision)\n\npackages/\n  host-runtime/rust/                 # crate `fgos-host-runtime` — the kernel\n    src/contracts.rs                 # OperationId, HostInvocation, OperationRequest, ProviderOutcome, ...\n    src/operation_provider_router.rs\n    src/invocation_service.rs\n    src/authority_gate.rs\n    src/providers/builtin.rs\n    src/remote_host_use_case.rs      # R3\n    src/chat_host_use_case.rs        # later\n    src/registry_linker.rs           # R2\n    src/providers/{external_process,external_wasm}.rs   # R2+\n  distribution/rust/                 # crate `fgos-distribution` — owns distribution.build.show\n  component-protocol/{rust,node}/    # R2: EncodedMessage, framed protocol\n\nbin/fgos.mjs, src/, scripts/, core/ ...   # the Node payload, unmoved (Legacy CLI Transition §2)\n```\n\nR1 is three crates: `fgos`, `fgos-host-runtime`, `fgos-distribution`. The legacy exec lane is a module inside `apps/fgos`, not a crate, because it is CLI-adapter-local (§4). `component-protocol` waits for R2 (only an external-process adapter needs `EncodedMessage`). Extract further crates only when pressure is real. Neither app owns provider selection; neither host use case imports another; every host feeds the shared authority/router/contracts layer, and provider adapters depend on component protocols, not host presentation. A component is not created merely because one proof verb is convenient (`gate-bypass` stays under its settled authority, not a manufactured `gate-policy` component).\n\nDistribution selects and activates the trusted runtime (`fgctl`: acquire/stage/verify/activate/upgrade/rollback); host invocation routes inside the activated runtime. Packaging-distribution owns the onboarding command vocabulary: local `fgos init` adopts a workspace under the active identity on first use, `fgos doctor --fix` performs every later registered repair, and the target architecture has no separate `setup` verb. See [Runtime Identity And Activation](../packaging-distribution/runtime-identity-and-activation.md)."

      "text": "## 9. Physical Placement",
      "sectionText": "## 9. Physical Placement\n\nThe public command name stays `fgos` — runtime identity is the release digest, not the name, and every skill, hook, plugin, and Herdr call already targets `fgos <verb>`. `fgctl` is a separate bootstrap binary, not a renamed `fgos`. Crate names are kebab-case with an `fgos-` prefix; modules are snake_case.\n\n```txt\nCargo.toml                           # workspace root; herdr-plugin/ excluded in R1\napps/\n  fgos/                              # crate `fgos`, binary `fgos` — thin CLI adapter\n    src/cli_projector.rs             # argv -> OperationRequest\n    src/cli_presenter.rs             # ProviderOutcome -> fgos.v1 / exit code\n    src/legacy_exec.rs               # CommandRouteDescriptor lookup + Node payload exec\n  gateway/                           # later: thin REST/MCP/remote adapter (repo-layout-vision)\n\npackages/\n  host-runtime/rust/                 # crate `fgos-host-runtime` — the kernel\n    src/contracts.rs                 # OperationId, HostInvocation, OperationRequest, ProviderOutcome, ...\n    src/operation_provider_router.rs\n    src/invocation_service.rs\n    src/authority_gate.rs\n    src/providers/builtin.rs\n    src/remote_host_use_case.rs      # R3\n    src/chat_host_use_case.rs        # later\n    src/registry_linker.rs           # R2\n    src/providers/{external_process,external_wasm}.rs   # R2+\n  distribution/rust/                 # crate `fgos-distribution` — owns distribution.build.show\n  component-protocol/{rust,node}/    # R2: EncodedMessage, framed protocol\n\nbin/fgos.mjs, src/, scripts/, core/ ...   # the Node payload, unmoved (Legacy CLI Transition §2)\n```\n\nR1 is three crates: `fgos`, `fgos-host-runtime`, `fgos-distribution`. The legacy exec lane is a module inside `apps/fgos`, not a crate, because it is CLI-adapter-local (§4). `component-protocol` waits for R2 (only an external-process adapter needs `EncodedMessage`). Extract further crates only when pressure is real. Neither app owns provider selection; neither host use case imports another; every host feeds the shared authority/router/contracts layer, and provider adapters depend on component protocols, not host presentation. A component is not created merely because one proof verb is convenient (`gate-bypass` stays under its settled authority, not a manufactured `gate-policy` component).\n\nDistribution selects and activates the trusted runtime (`fgctl`: acquire/stage/verify/activate/upgrade/rollback); host invocation routes inside the activated runtime. Packaging-distribution owns the onboarding command vocabulary: local `fgos init` adopts a workspace under the active identity on first use, `fgos doctor --fix` performs every later registered repair, and the target architecture has no separate `setup` verb. See [Runtime Identity And Activation](../packaging-distribution/runtime-identity-and-activation.md)."
    }
  },

    "sectionText": "#### 10. Release Boundaries\n\n| Release | Required architecture slice | Explicitly not a gate |\n|---|---|---|\n| R1 — distributable Rust CLI host | Invocation kernel; `const` `OperationCatalog` / `RegistrySnapshot` assembled once at the composition root; two-stage authority; transitional CLI lane in the CLI adapter; native `distribution.build.show`; `fgctl`-driven install/activate/rollback proof. | External ecosystem discovery, WASM, chat, production gateway migration, a `setup` verb. |\n| R2 — external process preview | Process protocol, supervision, fixture conformance, static manifest validation; one-shot CLI loads the derived cache by fingerprint, rebuilds only on mismatch; explicit test/dev roots. | Core replacement, signatures/marketplace, WASM. |\n| R3 — production remote peer | Remote projector/presenter, native route adoption, per-operation Node semantic bridge only where needed; remote peer is the **project-local gateway** (current herdr, same release) composing the host-runtime crate in-process. | Parsing CLI envelopes as internal API; a future **shared multi-project gateway**, which never links a project runtime in-process and instead reaches it through the out-of-process Project Runtime Adapter ([Future Constraints](../../architect/packaging-distribution/future-constraints.md) §2) — itself a `remote-host-use-case` adapter inside the project runtime. |\n\nChat is a valid future peer but does not gate R1/R2 until a real chat adapter and its admission/interruption/presentation contracts exist. \"Ship the Rust host\" means a reproducible artifact, target matrix, `fgctl` install/activation coverage, external-project install test, and named rollback channel — passing repository tests alone is a candidate, not a shipped host."
  },

    "followingBlockDigest": "3254fda9f7179fc52f68274cf803c9cfe550a6ea9f66d975cd3438100aaf804a",
    "identityFingerprint": "e3bba4f3dfed74b0c1b7218ce608018f3a3669dd97b409dc61670e2ebe9d0f4a",
    "ancestry": [

    "text": "#### 2. Legacy Payload Identity, Ownership, And Repair Path",
    "sectionText": "#### 2. Legacy Payload Identity, Ownership, And Repair Path\n\nThree things are separated that the name `bin/fgos.mjs` currently conflates:\n\n| | Today | After R1 |\n|---|---|---|\n| Public name people type | `fgos` → Node | `fgos` → Rust host (workspace shim / PATH) |\n| Payload identity the Rust host execs | none | `legacy-node` — the release manifest's `components.legacyNode` and the `legacy_payload` field of every `legacy-cli` `CommandRouteDescriptor` |\n| File location | `bin/fgos.mjs` at the repo root | unchanged |\n\n**The Node program is not relocated and not renamed in the source tree** (decided 2026-09-10). `bin/fgos.mjs` computes its package root from its own file location and imports `../src/...` relatively, so moving the entry alone breaks it, and moving the whole Node package would decide the Node-side repo layout that [Repo Layout Vision](../../../architect/component-boundary/repo-layout-vision.md) §7 deliberately defers (and would mislabel `src/state`, `src/runner` — which `fgos-runner` keeps using — as \"legacy\"). The payload is therefore the current npm package exactly as `package.json` `files` defines it, staged whole by the release builder under the manifest's `components.legacyNode.root` (`libexec/legacy-node/` in a staged release) with the same relative layout as the source tree — zero import changes, `bin/fgos.mjs` and `bin/fgos-runner.mjs` both inside it. The identity is renamed (`legacy-node`), the file is not; a filesystem rename happens only when the payload is deleted.\n\nThe public `fgos` executable is the platform Rust host. It resolves the legacy payload as `join(activeReleasePath, components.legacyNode.root, components.legacyNode.entry)` read from the activation binding's manifest — never from `PATH`, never from the caller's cwd, never as an alternate package-manager `bin` entry, and never hardcoded. A `dev:<rev>` source activation declares `root: \".\"`, `entry: \"bin/fgos.mjs\"`, `entries.fgos: \"target/release/fgos\"`; a staged release declares `root: \"libexec/legacy-node\"`, `entries.fgos: \"bin/fgos\"`. One mechanism serves dogfood and production ([Runtime Identity And Activation](../../../architect/packaging-distribution/runtime-identity-and-activation.md) §5).\n\nAdded in candidate — checked resolver status (2026-10-13): the preceding activation-binding paragraph is retained selected design. `apps/fgos/src/legacy_exec.rs:69-154` selects the release root from explicit release/dev environment bindings or executable-relative manifest discovery, then verifies the manifest and confined entry. The target identity status in spec.md remains `accepted-not-implemented`; checked resolver behavior does not certify the entire target contract. The ownership rule remains never from PATH, never from caller cwd, never as an alternate package-manager bin entry, and never hardcoded.\n\nAdded in candidate: this retained source detail is carried verbatim in [the dropped-010 restoration](release-boundaries.md#restored-package-json-bin-fgos-removed-pointed-at-workspace-shim-at-default-flip-bin-fgos-runner-stays-ownership-hea).\n\n\n**Callers of the old path.** A grep for `bin/fgos.mjs` finds ~150 hits; only ~9 are real call sites, all of them variants of \"where is `fgos`?\": the shell function's tier-1 (`scripts/fgos-shell-integration.sh`), Herdr's three `Command::new(\"node\")` sites (`fgos.rs`, `gateway.rs`, `main.rs`), the dispatch CLI path (`src/runner/dispatch/cli.mjs`), the iron-law footprint matcher (`src/evolve/iron-law.mjs`), the doctor reachability check (`src/setup/registrations.mjs`), the plugin-skill fallback (`core/skills/_shared/fgos-cli-fallback.md` — the single source the ~20 `.agents`/`plugins` copies render from), and `package.json` `bin`. The fix is not a substitution: add one **tier 0 = workspace shim `.fgos/installation/bin/fgos`** to the single resolver each runtime already has (`src/setup/bin-discovery.mjs` for Node, the shell function for shells, one `resolve_fgos` for Herdr) and make the nine sites use it, with the old `node bin/fgos.mjs` path kept only as the fallback for a project that has not run `fgctl init`. The ~75 Node tests that spawn `bin/fgos.mjs` directly stay as they are — they test the Node payload's behavior with the Node payload. Comments are not callers.\n\nEvery selector has exactly one generated `CommandRouteDescriptor`, derived from the Node command registry plus checked migration annotations. Its minimum fields:\n\n```txt\nselector               # canonical command/subcommand selector\nroute_kind             # legacy-cli | native\noperation_id           # required only for native semantic routing\nlegacy_payload         # required only for legacy-cli; named payload identity\nowner_path             # canonical implementation boundary to edit\ncompatibility_tests    # named parity/vector suites required for a repair\n```\n\n`legacy-cli` means the Node payload owns argument parsing and behavior; the Rust host must only recognize the checked selector and preserve the remaining `OsString` argv. `native` means the typed provider owns the operation and the legacy implementation is retained only as an explicitly bounded rollback oracle. A descriptor may not name both paths as active, and an unlisted selector fails the build rather than choosing a fallback.\n\nThe descriptor is both the routing input and the contributor repair map. A repository-local `scripts/explain-command-route.mjs <selector>` reads the same checked artifact and prints route kind, owner path, payload identity, and required compatibility suites. CI rejects a descriptor whose owner or required proof is missing, drift between the Node registry and descriptor, a direct production spawn of the private payload outside `LegacyCliPassthroughProvider` (test fixtures excepted), or a legacy payload removal before its compatibility binding is removed.\n\n**Rollback:** configuration can never replace a built-in provider (kernel contract §7), and there is no runtime provider-selection swap to roll back a native operation. Rollback of a native operation in R1–R2 is a **release rollback through `fgctl`** — the previous release still ships both the native provider and the Node payload during the observation window. There is no \"roll back by changing provider selection\" mechanism; none is promised anywhere in this stack."
  },

A descriptor may not name both paths as active, and an unlisted selector fails the build rather than choosing a fallback.\n\nThe descriptor is both the routing input and the contributor repair map. A repository-local `scripts/explain-command-route.mjs <selector>` reads the same checked artifact and prints route kind, owner path, payload identity, and required compatibility suites. CI rejects a descriptor whose owner or required proof is missing, drift between the Node registry and descriptor, a direct production spawn of the private payload outside `LegacyCliPassthroughProvider` (test fixtures excepted), or a legacy payload removal before its compatibility binding is removed.\n\n**Rollback:** configuration can never replace a built-in provider (kernel contract §7), and there is no runtime provider-selection swap to roll back a native operation. Rollback of a native operation in R1–R2 is a **release rollback through `fgctl`** — the previous release still ships both the native provider and the Node payload during the observation window. There is no \"roll back by changing provider selection\" mechanism; none is promised anywhere in this stack."

      "text": "#### 2. Legacy Payload Identity, Ownership, And Repair Path",
      "sectionText": "#### 2. Legacy Payload Identity, Ownership, And Repair Path\n\nThree things are separated that the name `bin/fgos.mjs` currently conflates:\n\n| | Today | After R1 |\n|---|---|---|\n| Public name people type | `fgos` → Node | `fgos` → Rust host (workspace shim / PATH) |\n| Payload identity the Rust host execs | none | `legacy-node` — the release manifest's `components.legacyNode` and the `legacy_payload` field of every `legacy-cli` `CommandRouteDescriptor` |\n| File location | `bin/fgos.mjs` at the repo root | unchanged |\n\n**The Node program is not relocated and not renamed in the source tree** (decided 2026-09-10). `bin/fgos.mjs` computes its package root from its own file location and imports `../src/...` relatively, so moving the entry alone breaks it, and moving the whole Node package would decide the Node-side repo layout that [Repo Layout Vision](../../../architect/component-boundary/repo-layout-vision.md) §7 deliberately defers (and would mislabel `src/state`, `src/runner` — which `fgos-runner` keeps using — as \"legacy\"). The payload is therefore the current npm package exactly as `package.json` `files` defines it, staged whole by the release builder under the manifest's `components.legacyNode.root` (`libexec/legacy-node/` in a staged release) with the same relative layout as the source tree — zero import changes, `bin/fgos.mjs` and `bin/fgos-runner.mjs` both inside it. The identity is renamed (`legacy-node`), the file is not; a filesystem rename happens only when the payload is deleted.\n\nThe public `fgos` executable is the platform Rust host. It resolves the legacy payload as `join(activeReleasePath, components.legacyNode.root, components.legacyNode.entry)` read from the activation binding's manifest — never from `PATH`, never from the caller's cwd, never as an alternate package-manager `bin` entry, and never hardcoded. A `dev:<rev>` source activation declares `root: \".\"`, `entry: \"bin/fgos.mjs\"`, `entries.fgos: \"target/release/fgos\"`; a staged release declares `root: \"libexec/legacy-node\"`, `entries.fgos: \"bin/fgos\"`. One mechanism serves dogfood and production ([Runtime Identity And Activation](../../../architect/packaging-distribution/runtime-identity-and-activation.md) §5).\n\nAdded in candidate — checked resolver status (2026-10-13): the preceding activation-binding paragraph is retained selected design. `apps/fgos/src/legacy_exec.rs:69-154` selects the release root from explicit release/dev environment bindings or executable-relative manifest discovery, then verifies the manifest and confined entry. The target identity status in spec.md remains `accepted-not-implemented`; checked resolver behavior does not certify the entire target contract. The ownership rule remains never from PATH, never from caller cwd, never as an alternate package-manager bin entry, and never hardcoded.\n\nAdded in candidate: this retained source detail is carried verbatim in [the dropped-010 restoration](release-boundaries.md#restored-package-json-bin-fgos-removed-pointed-at-workspace-shim-at-default-flip-bin-fgos-runner-stays-ownership-hea).\n\n\n**Callers of the old path.** A grep for `bin/fgos.mjs` finds ~150 hits; only ~9 are real call sites, all of them variants of \"where is `fgos`?\": the shell function's tier-1 (`scripts/fgos-shell-integration.sh`), Herdr's three `Command::new(\"node\")` sites (`fgos.rs`, `gateway.rs`, `main.rs`), the dispatch CLI path (`src/runner/dispatch/cli.mjs`), the iron-law footprint matcher (`src/evolve/iron-law.mjs`), the doctor reachability check (`src/setup/registrations.mjs`), the plugin-skill fallback (`core/skills/_shared/fgos-cli-fallback.md` — the single source the ~20 `.agents`/`plugins` copies render from), and `package.json` `bin`. The fix is not a substitution: add one **tier 0 = workspace shim `.fgos/installation/bin/fgos`** to the single resolver each runtime already has (`src/setup/bin-discovery.mjs` for Node, the shell function for shells, one `resolve_fgos` for Herdr) and make the nine sites use it, with the old `node bin/fgos.mjs` path kept only as the fallback for a project that has not run `fgctl init`. The ~75 Node tests that spawn `bin/fgos.mjs` directly stay as they are — they test the Node payload's behavior with the Node payload. Comments are not callers.\n\nEvery selector has exactly one generated `CommandRouteDescriptor`, derived from the Node command registry plus checked migration annotations. Its minimum fields:\n\n```txt\nselector               # canonical command/subcommand selector\nroute_kind             # legacy-cli | native\noperation_id           # required only for native semantic routing\nlegacy_payload         # required only for legacy-cli; named payload identity\nowner_path             # canonical implementation boundary to edit\ncompatibility_tests    # named parity/vector suites required for a repair\n```\n\n`legacy-cli` means the Node payload owns argument parsing and behavior; the Rust host must only recognize the checked selector and preserve the remaining `OsString` argv. `native` means the typed provider owns the operation and the legacy implementation is retained only as an explicitly bounded rollback oracle. A descriptor may not name both paths as active, and an unlisted selector fails the build rather than choosing a fallback.\n\nThe descriptor is both the routing input and the contributor repair map. A repository-local `scripts/explain-command-route.mjs <selector>` reads the same checked artifact and prints route kind, owner path, payload identity, and required compatibility suites. CI rejects a descriptor whose owner or required proof is missing, drift between the Node registry and descriptor, a direct production spawn of the private payload outside `LegacyCliPassthroughProvider` (test fixtures excepted), or a legacy payload removal before its compatibility binding is removed.\n\n**Rollback:** configuration can never replace a built-in provider (kernel contract §7), and there is no runtime provider-selection swap to roll back a native operation. Rollback of a native operation in R1–R2 is a **release rollback through `fgctl`** — the previous release still ships both the native provider and the Node payload during the observation window. There is no \"roll back by changing provider selection\" mechanism; none is promised anywhere in this stack."
    },

        "identityFingerprint": "fb7cc258dc05206d132fc94bb086f94b7c0cd11df20059cbcbe90b86c5a65e59",

          "Legacy CLI Transition"

        "text": "## 2. Legacy Payload Identity, Ownership, And Repair Path",
        "sectionText": "## 2. Legacy Payload Identity, Ownership, And Repair Path\n\nThree things are separated that the name `bin/fgos.mjs` currently conflates:\n\n| | Today | After R1 |\n|---|---|---|\n| Public name people type | `fgos` → Node | `fgos` → Rust host (workspace shim / PATH) |\n| Payload identity the Rust host execs | none | `legacy-node` — the release manifest's `components.legacyNode` and the `legacy_payload` field of every `legacy-cli` `CommandRouteDescriptor` |\n| File location | `bin/fgos.mjs` at the repo root | unchanged |\n\n**The Node program is not relocated and not renamed in the source tree** (decided 2026-09-10). `bin/fgos.mjs` computes its package root from its own file location and imports `../src/...` relatively, so moving the entry alone breaks it, and moving the whole Node package would decide the Node-side repo layout that [Repo Layout Vision](../component-boundary/repo-layout-vision.md) §7 deliberately defers (and would mislabel `src/state`, `src/runner` — which `fgos-runner` keeps using — as \"legacy\"). The payload is therefore the current npm package exactly as `package.json` `files` defines it, staged whole by the release builder under the manifest's `components.legacyNode.root` (`libexec/legacy-node/` in a staged release) with the same relative layout as the source tree — zero import changes, `bin/fgos.mjs` and `bin/fgos-runner.mjs` both inside it. The identity is renamed (`legacy-node`), the file is not; a filesystem rename happens only when the payload is deleted.\n\nThe public `fgos` executable is the platform Rust host. It resolves the legacy payload as `join(activeReleasePath, components.legacyNode.root, components.legacyNode.entry)` read from the activation binding's manifest — never from `PATH`, never from the caller's cwd, never as an alternate package-manager `bin` entry, and never hardcoded. A `dev:<rev>` source activation declares `root: \".\"`, `entry: \"bin/fgos.mjs\"`, `entries.fgos: \"target/release/fgos\"`; a staged release declares `root: \"libexec/legacy-node\"`, `entries.fgos: \"bin/fgos\"`. One mechanism serves dogfood and production ([Runtime Identity And Activation](../packaging-distribution/runtime-identity-and-activation.md) §5).\n\n`package.json` `bin.fgos` is removed (or pointed at the workspace shim) when the Rust host becomes the installed default; `bin.fgos-runner` stays until the runner migrates. A header in `bin/fgos.mjs` and the root `AGENTS.md` state the ownership rule for editors already at that path.\n\n**Callers of the old path.** A grep for `bin/fgos.mjs` finds ~150 hits; only ~9 are real call sites, all of them variants of \"where is `fgos`?\": the shell function's tier-1 (`scripts/fgos-shell-integration.sh`), Herdr's three `Command::new(\"node\")` sites (`fgos.rs`, `gateway.rs`, `main.rs`), the dispatch CLI path (`src/runner/dispatch/cli.mjs`), the iron-law footprint matcher (`src/evolve/iron-law.mjs`), the doctor reachability check (`src/setup/registrations.mjs`), the plugin-skill fallback (`core/skills/_shared/fgos-cli-fallback.md` — the single source the ~20 `.agents`/`plugins` copies render from), and `package.json` `bin`. The fix is not a substitution: add one **tier 0 = workspace shim `.fgos/installation/bin/fgos`** to the single resolver each runtime already has (`src/setup/bin-discovery.mjs` for Node, the shell function for shells, one `resolve_fgos` for Herdr) and make the nine sites use it, with the old `node bin/fgos.mjs` path kept only as the fallback for a project that has not run `fgctl init`. The ~75 Node tests that spawn `bin/fgos.mjs` directly stay as they are — they test the Node payload's behavior with the Node payload. Comments are not callers.\n\nEvery selector has exactly one generated `CommandRouteDescriptor`, derived from the Node command registry plus checked migration annotations. Its minimum fields:\n\n```txt\nselector               # canonical command/subcommand selector\nroute_kind             # legacy-cli | native\noperation_id           # required only for native semantic routing\nlegacy_payload         # required only for legacy-cli; named payload identity\nowner_path             # canonical implementation boundary to edit\ncompatibility_tests    # named parity/vector suites required for a repair\n```\n\n`legacy-cli` means the Node payload owns argument parsing and behavior; the Rust host must only recognize the checked selector and preserve the remaining `OsString` argv. `native` means the typed provider owns the operation and the legacy implementation is retained only as an explicitly bounded rollback oracle. A descriptor may not name both paths as active, and an unlisted selector fails the build rather than choosing a fallback.\n\nThe descriptor is both the routing input and the contributor repair map. A repository-local `scripts/explain-command-route.mjs <selector>` reads the same checked artifact and prints route kind, owner path, payload identity, and required compatibility suites. CI rejects a descriptor whose owner or required proof is missing, drift between the Node registry and descriptor, a direct production spawn of the private payload outside `LegacyCliPassthroughProvider` (test fixtures excepted), or a legacy payload removal before its compatibility binding is removed.\n\n**Rollback:** configuration can never replace a built-in provider (kernel contract §7), and there is no runtime provider-selection swap to roll back a native operation. Rollback of a native operation in R1–R2 is a **release rollback through `fgctl`** — the previous release still ships both the native provider and the Node payload during the observation window. There is no \"roll back by changing provider selection\" mechanism; none is promised anywhere in this stack."
      }
    },

    "text": "#### 5. Release R1: Distributable Rust CLI Host",
    "sectionText": "#### 5. Release R1: Distributable Rust CLI Host\n\nR1 is the smallest honest meaning of “ship the Rust host”. It is not merely a\nbinary that passes repository tests. The installed product entry becomes Rust,\nall unmigrated CLI selectors retain transparent whole-invocation Node\ncompatibility, `fgos-runner` remains a separately proven Node public entry, and\n`version` proves one typed built-in operation.\n\nThe migration order is:\n\n1. adopt the packaging stream's settled install/activation/rollback contract\n   (`fgctl` + release store + workspace activation binding; see\n   [Runtime Identity And Activation](../../../architect/packaging-distribution/runtime-identity-and-activation.md)\n   §11–§13); confirm the supported target matrix;\n2. name the Node payload `legacy-node` in the release manifest\n   (`components.legacyNode.root`/`entry`) without moving or renaming any file;\n   add the ownership header to `bin/fgos.mjs` and the root `AGENTS.md` note;\n3. freeze executable Node compatibility evidence and the checked command-route\n   descriptor, including the owner and test suite for every selector;\n4. land the Rust invocation kernel with immutable static bindings and the\n   two-stage authority path;\n5. wire the CLI adapter to read the checked `CommandRouteDescriptor` for every\n   current selector: a `legacy-cli` selector execs straight to the Node\n   payload with argv preserved, never entering `InvocationService`; only a\n   `native` selector builds an `OperationRequest`. See\n   [Legacy CLI Transition](legacy-cli-transition.md);\n6. migrate `version` to native `distribution.build.show`;\n7. prove the install/activation/rollback contract through `fgctl init` on an\n   external temp project from a staged release, followed by the active\n   runtime's `fgos init` → `doctor --fix` → `doctor`, on every supported\n   target;\n8. flip the installed default only after the compatibility and distribution\n   gates pass.\n\nExternal-process discovery, WASM, chat, and production gateway adoption do not\nblock R1. They prove later parts of the permanent architecture without delaying\nthe first usable release.\n\nExit condition: every existing CLI invocation still reaches Node unchanged (via\nthe CLI adapter's legacy-cli exec lane) or an explicitly native provider,\n`version` creates no Node process, and the proof runs through `fgctl init` on\nan external temp project from a staged release, followed by the active\nruntime's `fgos init` → `doctor --fix` → `doctor`, with the previous release\nremaining a named rollback channel through `fgctl`. For every legacy selector,\n`explain-command-route` identifies the canonical Node owner and required\nparity suite; no contributor must infer ownership from a stale `bin/fgos.mjs`\nreference. The activated Rust host, legacy payload, and Node runner always\ncome from one versioned release artifact; no release mixes them across\nversions."
  },

      "text": "#### 5. Release R1: Distributable Rust CLI Host",
      "sectionText": "#### 5. Release R1: Distributable Rust CLI Host\n\nR1 is the smallest honest meaning of “ship the Rust host”. It is not merely a\nbinary that passes repository tests. The installed product entry becomes Rust,\nall unmigrated CLI selectors retain transparent whole-invocation Node\ncompatibility, `fgos-runner` remains a separately proven Node public entry, and\n`version` proves one typed built-in operation.\n\nThe migration order is:\n\n1. adopt the packaging stream's settled install/activation/rollback contract\n   (`fgctl` + release store + workspace activation binding; see\n   [Runtime Identity And Activation](../../../architect/packaging-distribution/runtime-identity-and-activation.md)\n   §11–§13); confirm the supported target matrix;\n2. name the Node payload `legacy-node` in the release manifest\n   (`components.legacyNode.root`/`entry`) without moving or renaming any file;\n   add the ownership header to `bin/fgos.mjs` and the root `AGENTS.md` note;\n3. freeze executable Node compatibility evidence and the checked command-route\n   descriptor, including the owner and test suite for every selector;\n4. land the Rust invocation kernel with immutable static bindings and the\n   two-stage authority path;\n5. wire the CLI adapter to read the checked `CommandRouteDescriptor` for every\n   current selector: a `legacy-cli` selector execs straight to the Node\n   payload with argv preserved, never entering `InvocationService`; only a\n   `native` selector builds an `OperationRequest`. See\n   [Legacy CLI Transition](legacy-cli-transition.md);\n6. migrate `version` to native `distribution.build.show`;\n7. prove the install/activation/rollback contract through `fgctl init` on an\n   external temp project from a staged release, followed by the active\n   runtime's `fgos init` → `doctor --fix` → `doctor`, on every supported\n   target;\n8. flip the installed default only after the compatibility and distribution\n   gates pass.\n\nExternal-process discovery, WASM, chat, and production gateway adoption do not\nblock R1. They prove later parts of the permanent architecture without delaying\nthe first usable release.\n\nExit condition: every existing CLI invocation still reaches Node unchanged (via\nthe CLI adapter's legacy-cli exec lane) or an explicitly native provider,\n`version` creates no Node process, and the proof runs through `fgctl init` on\nan external temp project from a staged release, followed by the active\nruntime's `fgos init` → `doctor --fix` → `doctor`, with the previous release\nremaining a named rollback channel through `fgctl`. For every legacy selector,\n`explain-command-route` identifies the canonical Node owner and required\nparity suite; no contributor must infer ownership from a stale `bin/fgos.mjs`\nreference. The activated Rust host, legacy payload, and Node runner always\ncome from one versioned release artifact; no release mixes them across\nversions."
    },

For every legacy selector,\n`explain-command-route` identifies the canonical Node owner and required\nparity suite; no contributor must infer ownership from a stale `bin/fgos.mjs`\nreference. The activated Rust host, legacy payload, and Node runner always\ncome from one versioned release artifact; no release mixes them across\nversions."
    }
  },

    "text": "#### 7. Release R3: Production Remote Host",
    "sectionText": "#### 7. Release R3: Production Remote Host\n\nAdopt the common invocation service route by route:\n\n1. inventory current gateway routes by semantic operation and side effect;\n2. replace `VerbGateway` for one native read with a remote projector and\n   presenter calling the shared invocation service;\n3. keep REST/MCP authentication and transport presentation in the gateway;\n4. for a route that must remain on Node, build a real per-operation Node\n   semantic bridge or leave that route on the old chokepoint during its named\n   rollback window;\n5. never parse `fgos.v1` or captured CLI stdout as the remote internal API;\n6. delete the CLI-shelling chokepoint after no route uses it.\n\nCaptured/supervised legacy CLI output is not a semantic provider outcome and\ncannot serve this stage. This stage gets a separate blast-radius review because\nthe current Herdr crate combines gateway, TUI, Axum, MCP, auth, and web concerns.\n\nThe production remote host in R3 is the project-local gateway (the current\nHerdr crate, released alongside the runtime) composing the host-runtime crate\nin-process. A future shared multi-project gateway is a different component: it\nreaches a selected project runtime only through the out-of-process Project\nRuntime Adapter\n([Future Constraints](../../../architect/packaging-distribution/future-constraints.md) §2),\nnever by loading a project runtime in-process itself.\n\nChat becomes a peer host only when a real chat adapter and its own contracts\nexist. Host extensibility is preserved meanwhile; a speculative chat proof is\nnot a release gate."
  },

    "text": "#### 13. Rollback Rules",
    "sectionText": "#### 13. Rollback Rules\n\nConfig can never replace a built-in provider (host doc open question 2 closed\nas \"prohibit\"). A provider binding is not a runtime-selectable switch, so\nrollback of a native operation in R1–R2 is a release rollback through `fgctl`:\n`ActivationRecord.previousArtifactDigest` + the preserved release directory +\na state-schema compatibility check (see\n[Runtime Identity And Activation](../../../architect/packaging-distribution/runtime-identity-and-activation.md)\n§11). The previous release still contains both the native provider and the\nNode payload during the operation's observation window, so a release rollback\nrestores the legacy path without restoring the old outer executable by hand.\n\n\nAdded in candidate: this retained source detail is carried verbatim in [the dropped-015 restoration](../contracts/component-protocol.md#restored-rollback-bullets)."
  },

        "text": "## 13. Rollback Rules",
        "sectionText": "## 13. Rollback Rules\n\nConfig can never replace a built-in provider (host doc open question 2 closed\nas \"prohibit\"). A provider binding is not a runtime-selectable switch, so\nrollback of a native operation in R1–R2 is a release rollback through `fgctl`:\n`ActivationRecord.previousArtifactDigest` + the preserved release directory +\na state-schema compatibility check (see\n[Runtime Identity And Activation](../packaging-distribution/runtime-identity-and-activation.md)\n§11). The previous release still contains both the native provider and the\nNode payload during the operation's observation window, so a release rollback\nrestores the legacy path without restoring the old outer executable by hand.\n\n- Keep legacy and native implementations side by side only for the observation\n  window of their operation.\n- Never delete a Node writer before proving it can read/recover state last\n  written by the Rust implementation, or explicitly declaring the cutover\n  irreversible with migration evidence.\n- Remove rollback code per component after its window; do not accumulate a\n  permanent second implementation tree."
      }

      "sectionText": "#### 15. Remaining Migration Decisions\n\n1. Which supported target matrix gates the first distributed Rust host?\n2. How long is the provider rollback observation window?\n3.     "text": "### Rust Host And Proof Providers Implementation Plan",
    "sectionText": "### Rust Host And Proof Providers Implementation Plan\n\n**Status:** Proposed execution plan; blocked only by the remaining §3 decisions\n(target matrix, preview-vs-stable, compatibility-window duration) and the\npackaging stream's `fgctl` walking skeleton (§4, node `PK`).\n**Date:** 2026-09-04.\n**Revised:** 2026-09-10 (see plans/reports/architecture-review-260910-1537-host-invocation-provider-routing-design-review.md).\n**Architecture:** [Host Invocation And Provider Routing](spec.md).\n**Migration strategy:** [Node To Rust Component Migration](architecture/node-to-rust-migration.md).\n**Component placement:** [fgOS Component Boundary Advisory](../../architect/component-boundary/component-boundary-advisory.md).\n**Distribution/activation authority:** [Runtime Identity And Activation](../../architect/packaging-distribution/runtime-identity-and-activation.md); this plan consumes that stream's walking skeleton, it does not redefine install/activation.\n\nThis document contains execution order, deliverables, gates, verification, and\nrollback.     "text": "#### 3. Roots And On-Disk Shape",
    "sectionText": "#### 3. Roots And On-Disk Shape\n\nThe root topology is defined in\n[Workspace Topology Architecture](../../../architect/workspace-topology.md). This document uses\nthat topology and focuses on runtime identity records.\n\nThe minimum shape is:\n\n\n```txt\nworkspace root:\n  .fgos/\n    config.json             # tracked workspace/branch policy\n    distribution.json       # tracked team/project pin\n    installation/\n      bin/\n        fgos                # ignored stable workspace shim\n        fgos-runner         # ignored stable workspace shim\n      root.json             # ignored TopologyContext/root binding snapshot\n      activation.json       # ignored per-workspace ready binding\n      projections/\n        ledger.json         # ignored per-workspace projection ledger\n\nworkHistoryRoot(workStateId):\n  active-events/            # hot durable history; physical placement owned by topology/work-state\n  schema.json               # current work-state schema record\n  derived/\n\nruntimeCoordinationRoot(workStateId):\n  claims/\n  sessions/\n  leases/\n  locks/\n\nmachineReleaseStore:\n  releases/\n    <artifactDigest>/\n      manifest.json\n      bin/\n        fgos\n        fgos-runner\n      libexec/\n        legacy-node/\n      workshop/\n        skills/\n        agents/\n        prose/\n      docs/\n  installs/\n    <activationId>.json\n  install.lock\n  quarantine/\n```\n\nThe separation is architectural:\n\n- release store `releases/<artifactDigest>/` is immutable release payload;\n- workspace `.fgos/installation/bin/*` is the stable local entry surface;\n- workspace `.fgos/installation/activation.json` selects the active runtime for\n  that workspace only;\n- workspace `.fgos/config.json` is tracked workspace/branch policy;\n- workspace `.fgos/distribution.json` is tracked runtime pin policy and may\n  differ by branch/worktree;\n- workspace `.fgos/installation/projections/ledger.json` records projections for\n  that workspace only;\n- `workHistoryRoot(workStateId)` owns durable workflow history, not packaging;\n- `runtimeCoordinationRoot(workStateId)` owns claims/sessions/leases/locks and\n  must not share a namespace with release/activation records;\n- config, event history, coordination, cache, activation, and projections have\n  distinct state classes per\n  [Workspace Topology Architecture](../../../architect/workspace-topology.md).\n\nWorker workspaces still need an installation capsule if commands are expected\nto enter through local shims. They must not symlink or copy the entire shared\n`.fgos` state tree. The minimum worker capsule is:\n\n```txt\nworker workspace:\n  .fgos/\n    distribution.json        # checked out with the branch when present\n    installation/\n      bin/fgos\n      bin/fgos-runner\n      root.json              # binds shared workState/release/coordination roots\n      activation.json\n      projections/ledger.json\n```\n\nIf `.fgos/distribution.json` exists but the release store has not staged its\nrequested release, the workspace is in `pinned-not-staged`. `fgctl init` must\nacquire/stage the pinned release and publish this workspace's activation\nbinding, not silently choose latest.\n\nPossible tracked pin shape:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"schemaVersion\": 1,\n  \"projectRuntime\": {\n    \"policy\": \"exact-digest\",\n    \"artifactDigest\": \"sha256:...\",\n    \"releaseVersion\": \"0.1.0\",\n    \"channel\": null,\n    \"allowPrerelease\": false\n  }\n}\n```\n\nRoot resolution order for the stable shim:\n\n```txt\n1. read workspace .fgos/installation/root.json if present;\n2. otherwise resolve TopologyContext for repository/workspace/work-state identity;\n3. read machineReleaseStore from TopologyContext;\n4. read workspace .fgos/installation/activation.json;\n5. exec releases/<artifactDigest>/bin/<entry>.\n```\n\nThe shim must not treat a shared release store as a shared active runtime. Two\nworktrees may use different activation bindings while sharing the same\ncontent-addressed releases.\n\n`<artifactDigest>` is a path-safe digest identity for the canonical release\ntree manifest, for example `sha256-abc123...`. It is not the path humans,\nagents, gateway, or runner supervisors should call directly. The stable command\npath is:\n\n```txt\n.fgos/installation/bin/fgos\n.fgos/installation/bin/fgos-runner\n```\n\nThose entries are thin local shims. A shim should do only the minimum required\nto enter the active release:\n\n```txt\nresolve machineReleaseStore from TopologyContext/root binding\nread workspace .fgos/installation/activation.json\nresolve artifactDigest to releases/<digest>/\nverify the target entry exists\nexec the active release binary\n```\n\nIt must not scan the full workspace, verify every fingerprint, resolve network\nversions, run doctor checks, or load broad registries on every command. Full\nverification belongs to install/repair/doctor paths. The normal command\noverhead should be limited to reading one small record and executing the active\nbinary.\n\nShim forward-compatibility rule: the shim reads only `schemaVersion`,\n`artifactDigest`, and `releasePath` from workspace `activation.json`. Broader\nactivation metadata may evolve without requiring every stable shim to be\nreplaced.\n\nThe alternative is a `current` symlink, but the preferred V1 is a shim because\nit works more consistently on Windows, can produce clear errors when the active\nrelease is missing, and can later add a lightweight invocation lease without\ndepending on filesystem symlink behavior."
  },

      "sectionText": "## 3. Roots And On-Disk Shape\n\nThe root topology is defined in\n[Workspace Topology Architecture](../workspace-topology.md). This document uses\nthat topology and focuses on runtime identity records.\n\nThe minimum shape is:\n\n\n```txt\nworkspace root:\n  .fgos/\n    config.json             # tracked workspace/branch policy\n    distribution.json       # tracked team/project pin\n    installation/\n      bin/\n        fgos                # ignored stable workspace shim\n        fgos-runner         # ignored stable workspace shim\n      root.json             # ignored TopologyContext/root binding snapshot\n      activation.json       # ignored per-workspace ready binding\n      projections/\n        ledger.json         # ignored per-workspace projection ledger\n\nworkHistoryRoot(workStateId):\n  active-events/            # hot durable history; physical placement owned by topology/work-state\n  schema.json               # current work-state schema record\n  derived/\n\nruntimeCoordinationRoot(workStateId):\n  claims/\n  sessions/\n  leases/\n  locks/\n\nmachineReleaseStore:\n  releases/\n    <artifactDigest>/\n      manifest.json\n      bin/\n        fgos\n        fgos-runner\n      libexec/\n        legacy-node/\n      workshop/\n        skills/\n        agents/\n        prose/\n      docs/\n  installs/\n    <activationId>.json\n  install.lock\n  quarantine/\n```\n\nThe separation is architectural:\n\n- release store `releases/<artifactDigest>/` is immutable release payload;\n- workspace `.fgos/installation/bin/*` is the stable local entry surface;\n- workspace `.fgos/installation/activation.json` selects the active runtime for\n  that workspace only;\n- workspace `.fgos/config.json` is tracked workspace/branch policy;\n- workspace `.fgos/distribution.json` is tracked runtime pin policy and may\n  differ by branch/worktree;\n- workspace `.fgos/installation/projections/ledger.json` records projections for\n  that workspace only;\n- `workHistoryRoot(workStateId)` owns durable workflow history, not packaging;\n- `runtimeCoordinationRoot(workStateId)` owns claims/sessions/leases/locks and\n  must not share a namespace with release/activation records;\n- config, event history, coordination, cache, activation, and projections have\n  distinct state classes per\n  [Workspace Topology Architecture](../workspace-topology.md).\n\nWorker workspaces still need an installation capsule if commands are expected\nto enter through local shims. They must not symlink or copy the entire shared\n`.fgos` state tree. The minimum worker capsule is:\n\n```txt\nworker workspace:\n  .fgos/\n    distribution.json        # checked out with the branch when present\n    installation/\n      bin/fgos\n      bin/fgos-runner\n      root.json              # binds shared workState/release/coordination roots\n      activation.json\n      projections/ledger.json\n```\n\nIf `.fgos/distribution.json` exists but the release store has not staged its\nrequested release, the workspace is in `pinned-not-staged`. `fgctl init` must\nacquire/stage the pinned release and publish this workspace's activation\nbinding, not silently choose latest.\n\nPossible tracked pin shape:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"schemaVersion\": 1,\n  \"projectRuntime\": {\n    \"policy\": \"exact-digest\",\n    \"artifactDigest\": \"sha256:...\",\n    \"releaseVersion\": \"0.1.0\",\n    \"channel\": null,\n    \"allowPrerelease\": false\n  }\n}\n```\n\nRoot resolution order for the stable shim:\n\n```txt\n1. read workspace .fgos/installation/root.json if present;\n2. otherwise resolve TopologyContext for repository/workspace/work-state identity;\n3. read machineReleaseStore from TopologyContext;\n4. read workspace .fgos/installation/activation.json;\n5. exec releases/<artifactDigest>/bin/<entry>.\n```\n\nThe shim must not treat a shared release store as a shared active runtime. Two\nworktrees may use different activation bindings while sharing the same\ncontent-addressed releases.\n\n`<artifactDigest>` is a path-safe digest identity for the canonical release\ntree manifest, for example `sha256-abc123...`. It is not the path humans,\nagents, gateway, or runner supervisors should call directly. The stable command\npath is:\n\n```txt\n.fgos/installation/bin/fgos\n.fgos/installation/bin/fgos-runner\n```\n\nThose entries are thin local shims. A shim should do only the minimum required\nto enter the active release:\n\n```txt\nresolve machineReleaseStore from TopologyContext/root binding\nread workspace .fgos/installation/activation.json\nresolve artifactDigest to releases/<digest>/\nverify the target entry exists\nexec the active release binary\n```\n\nIt must not scan the full workspace, verify every fingerprint, resolve network\nversions, run doctor checks, or load broad registries on every command. Full\nverification belongs to install/repair/doctor paths. The normal command\noverhead should be limited to reading one small record and executing the active\nbinary.\n\nShim forward-compatibility rule: the shim reads only `schemaVersion`,\n`artifactDigest`, and `releasePath` from workspace `activation.json`. Broader\nactivation metadata may evolve without requiring every stable shim to be\nreplaced.\n\nThe alternative is a `current` symlink, but the preferred V1 is a shim because\nit works more consistently on Windows, can produce clear errors when the active\nrelease is missing, and can later add a lightweight invocation lease without\ndepending on filesystem symlink behavior."
    }
  },
  "A36ClassObservation": {
    "class": "Judgment",
    "reason": "no target digest match",
    "targetUnit": null
  },

}

      "text": "- release store `releases/<artifactDigest>/` is immutable release payload;\n- workspace `.fgos/installation/bin/*` is the stable local entry surface;\n- workspace `.fgos/installation/activation.json` selects the active runtime for\n  that workspace only;\n- workspace `.fgos/config.json` is tracked workspace/branch policy;\n- workspace `.fgos/distribution.json` is tracked runtime pin policy and may\n  differ by branch/worktree;\n- workspace `.fgos/installation/projections/ledger.json` records projections for\n  that workspace only;\n- `workHistoryRoot(workStateId)` owns durable workflow history, not packaging;\n- `runtimeCoordinationRoot(workStateId)` owns claims/sessions/leases/locks and\n  must not share a namespace with release/activation records;\n- config, event history, coordination, cache, activation, and projections have\n  distinct state classes per\n  [Workspace Topology Architecture](../workspace-topology.md)."

    "sectionText": "#### 5. ReleaseManifest\n\nThe release manifest is the immutable statement of what an fgOS release\ncontains.\n\nThe canonical artifact digest is computed from this release tree manifest, not\nfrom a `.zip`, `.tar.gz`, npm package archive, or transport wrapper. Archive\ndigests may still be recorded for download/integrity diagnostics, but they are\nnot runtime identity. Runtime identity must survive different compression\nformats, package transports, and mirror locations.\n\nThe digest formula is:\n\n```txt\nfileDigest = sha256(file bytes as emitted by the release build)\nartifactDigest = sha256(canonical-json(release tree manifest without artifactDigest))\n```\n\nThe release build, not the installer, owns byte normalization. Install should\nnot rewrite line endings or file contents to make a digest pass.\n\nMinimum fields:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"schemaVersion\": 1,\n  \"artifactDigest\": \"sha256:...\",\n  \"digestKind\": \"release-tree-manifest\",\n  \"releaseVersion\": \"0.1.0\",\n  \"sourceRevision\": \"...\",\n  \"createdAt\": \"2026-09-04T00:00:00Z\",\n  \"target\": {\n    \"os\": \"linux\",\n    \"arch\": \"x64\",\n    \"libc\": \"glibc\"\n  },\n  \"entries\": {\n    \"fgos\": \"bin/fgos\",\n    \"fgosRunner\": \"bin/fgos-runner\"\n  },\n  \"components\": {\n    \"legacyNode\": {\n      \"root\": \"libexec/legacy-node\",\n      \"entry\": \"bin/fgos.mjs\",\n      \"digest\": \"sha256:...\"\n    },\n    \"runner\": {\n      \"path\": \"bin/fgos-runner\",\n      \"digest\": \"sha256:...\"\n    },\n    \"workshop\": {\n      \"skillsDigest\": \"sha256:...\",\n      \"agentsDigest\": \"sha256:...\",\n      \"proseDigest\": \"sha256:...\"\n    }\n  },\n  \"requires\": {\n    \"node\": \">=20 <23\",\n    \"git\": \">=2.39\"\n  },\n  \"adapter\": {\n    \"protocolVersion\": \"1\",\n    \"entry\": \"bin/fgos adapter\",\n    \"capabilities\": []\n  },\n  \"stateSchemas\": {\n    \"read\": [\"1\"],\n    \"write\": [\"1\"],\n    \"migrations\": []\n  },\n  \"files\": []\n}\n```\n\n`components.legacyNode` names a payload **root** plus an **entry** inside it, not a single file (proposed 2026-09-10 by the host-invocation stream, see [Legacy CLI Transition](../../../architect/host-invocation-routing/legacy-cli-transition.md) §2): the legacy payload is the whole Node package as `package.json` `files` defines it, staged with its source-relative layout intact so `bin/fgos.mjs` needs no import changes, and `bin/fgos-runner.mjs` lives in the same root. The Rust host resolves `join(activeReleasePath, root, entry)` and nothing else. A `dev:<rev>` source activation declares `root: \".\"`, `entry: \"bin/fgos.mjs\"`, `entries.fgos: \"target/release/fgos\"` — the same fields serve dogfood and a staged release."
  },

      "sectionText": "## 2. Historical Document Split\n\nThis discussion proposed the split below. The active promoted split now lives\nunder `docs/platform/packaging-distribution/**`.\n\n```txt\ndocs/architect/\n  workspace-topology.md\n    repository/workspace/work-state identities, state classes, modes,\n    operation-to-root matrix, lifecycle/failure modes, dirty-tree rules\n\ndocs/architect/packaging-distribution/\n  README.md\n    discussion spine and target model later promoted to platform docs\n\n  scope-map.md\n    this file; concern map and document routing\n\n  runtime-identity-and-activation.md\n    immutable release manifest, workspace activation binding, pin, projection\n    ledger, migration journal outline, invocation lease, drift, rollback,\n    quarantine\n\n  future-constraints.md\n    future shared web/gateway constraint, Project Runtime Adapter,\n    out-of-process protocol, global substrate boundary\n\n  history/distribution-baseline.md\n    old Node/npm baseline and generated-spec fragments preserved as input\n\nfuture optional splits, only when they outgrow runtime identity:\n  fgctl-and-local-fgos-contract.md\n  workshop-materialization.md\n```\n\n[Workspace Topology Architecture](../workspace-topology.md) must be read before\nruntime identity, because packaging consumes topology rather than owning it.\n[Runtime Identity And Activation](../../platform/packaging-distribution/architecture/runtime-identity-and-activation.md)\nis the promoted first packaging-specific contract. Gateway/web itself is not\nactive delivery scope; its constraints live in\n[Future Constraints](../../platform/packaging-distribution/architecture/future-constraints.md)."
    }
  },

    "text": "## 13. Migration Rule",
    "sectionText": "## 13. Migration Rule\n\nDo not bulk-move old docs before classifying them by type, authority, lifecycle,\nprovenance, and claim ownership. Content may be transformed and reviewed one\narea at a time, but the authorized migration program must declare whether\npromotion is per-area or repository-wide; transformation order alone never\nchanges authority.\n\nUntil a newer program is explicitly accepted, each area portal's current-source\nmapping controls, operationalized through [transitional-switchboard.md](../transitional-switchboard.md).\nAuthors during migration must follow [platform/migration-authoring-rules.md](migration-authoring-rules.md)\n(one claim, one canonical owner, never dual-author prose, ratchet enforcement on legacy roots).\nA target marked partial/candidate does not outrank that map, and readers must surface\nconflicts rather than infer authority from path or date. Any redirect/stub must be\nexplicitly read-only and temporary. The proposed repository-wide normalization and\nalias-based retirement model is documented in\n`platform/proposals/documentation-system-unification.md` and is not active merely\nbecause its plan exists."
  },

    "text": "## 13. Migration Rule",
    "sectionText": "## 13. Migration Rule\n\nDo not bulk-move old docs before classifying them by type, authority, lifecycle,\nprovenance, and claim ownership. Content may be transformed and reviewed one\narea at a time, but the authorized migration program must declare whether\npromotion is per-area or repository-wide; transformation order alone never\nchanges authority.\n\nUntil a newer program is explicitly accepted, each area portal's current-source\nmapping controls, operationalized through [transitional-switchboard.md](documentation/switchboard.md).\nAuthors during migration must follow [platform/migration-authoring-rules.md](migration-authoring-rules.md)\n(one claim, one canonical owner, never dual-author prose, ratchet enforcement on legacy roots).\nA target marked partial/candidate does not outrank that map, and readers must surface\nconflicts rather than infer authority from path or date. Any redirect/stub must be\nexplicitly read-only and temporary. The proposed repository-wide normalization and\nalias-based retirement model is documented in\n`platform/proposals/documentation-system-unification.md` and is not active merely\nbecause its plan exists."
  },

      "text": "## 0.1 System-Wide Vision",
      "sectionText": "## 0.1 System-Wide Vision\n\n[System Vision: Trong Mem Ngoai Cung](system-vision-trong-mem-ngoai-cung.md)\nis the cross-system reminder behind this intent file:\n\n```txt\nOutside hard:\n  contract, state, capability, topology, proof, audit\n\nInside soft:\n  soul, prose, skill, judgment, collaboration, domain intelligence\n```\n\nStep 09 showed why this reminder is necessary.     "text": "## 17. MVP Roadmap",
    "sectionText": "## 17. MVP Roadmap\n\nThis is the plan shape, not a menu of questions. Each MVP keeps the original\nintention alive while adding only the architecture needed for that layer. The\ndetailed proposal lives in\n[Step 09 - Group Thinking Substrate](../../../architect/proposals/step-09-group-thinking-substrate.md).\n\nStable spine:\n\n```txt\nFlowDefinition = static legality envelope\nCoordinationSession = event-sourced runtime ledger\nExternal driver = adaptive authority outside the worker graph\nAssignment / Run / RunResult = execution and evidence path\nContext grant = visibility and memory access path\nSkill / surface = thin launcher only\n```\n\n| MVP | Goal | Real shape | Architecture change | Proof |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 0 | Shape lock. | Record the stable spine and boundaries before runtime work. | Docs-only. | Link/check review; no runtime/schema edit. |\n| 1 | Standalone Master Coordination fixture. | `plan.md` or `artifact.md` enters a declared worker graph: Doer, Reviewer, Red-Team, Fixer/Doer-followup, optional Synthesizer. Doer/Fixer produce session-local artifacts/revisions. | Fixture draft first; schema validation after acceptance. | Static skeleton expresses Master Coordination without Work fields or git authority. |\n| 2 | Driver authorization primitive. | Optional operations require `operation-authorized` before dispatch, with `authorizationId`, `operationId`, `targetActorId`, `invocationKey`, `authorizedBy`, `reason`, `grantedContextRefs`, and `artifactRevision`. | Schema/runtime after acceptance. | Missing authorization, undeclared operation, over-cap invocation, terminal-session authorization, and context beyond grant are rejected. |\n| 3 | Recheck and disposition. | Recheck is a new Assignment against a new artifact revision; disposition is a driver event, not worker self-report. | Schema/runtime after MVP 2. | Old verdict remains immutable; new verdict links to revision; synthesis preserves dissent and unresolved findings. |\n| 4 | Surface launcher. | A skill/slash surface builds a request for a declared fixture and calls `fgos coordination run --file`, then reads `coordination show`/evidence. | Surface only; no group-thinking logic inside the skill. | Launcher cannot bypass FlowDefinition/session authorization. |\n| 5 | Live standalone proof. | Run the Master Coordination loop with no Work: input plan, Doer artifact, Reviewer report, Red-Team report, driver-authorized fix, revision, recheck, final disposition. | CLI/headless run. | CLI/headless parity, crash/resume no duplicate, unauthorized optional operation rejected, hidden context rejected, bounds enforced. |\n| 6 | Visibility windows. | Topology declares fail-closed private-first-pass and post-independent-pass windows; operation bindings select a window; authorization and Assignment provenance retain exact `grantedContextRefs`. | Deferred schema/runtime. | Opt-in fixtures share only eligible same-session artifact refs after the milestone; unchanged isolation fixtures still reject sibling leakage. |\n| 7 | Evidence-preserving aggregation. | Keep completion eligibility separate from one `evidence-preserving-synthesis` method whose validated outcome is `consensus`, `qualified`, or `no-consensus`. | Deferred schema/runtime plus Team Cognition boundary. | Aggregate output cannot hide source coverage, dissent, unresolved objections, failed/missing actors, or artifact revisions, and cannot upgrade evidence confidence. |\n| 8 | Deliberation memory. | Link immutable, artifact-backed `proposal`, `objection`, `response`, `clarification`, `rank`, and `specialist-request` contributions into the session ledger. | Deferred schema/runtime. | Replay preserves contribution lineage without recipient, inbox, unread, delivery, or arbitrary message-body semantics. |\n| 9 | Bounded dynamic specialist pull-in. | The driver binds one specialist into a predeclared, capability- and assignment-capped specialist slot, then uses existing operation authorization. | Deferred schema/runtime. | Opt-in fixture accepts the bounded binding; undeclared slots, over-cap binding, foreign context, unauthorized writers, and unchanged isolation fixtures reject it. |\n\nAfter MVP9, concrete RFC-lite, Nominal-Group-lite, and Delphi-feedback-lite\ndefinitions belong in an external **Group-Thinking Protocol Pack**. A\n**Group-Thinking Conformance Suite** proves those definitions use only public\ncontracts, and a thin `fgos-group-thinking` skill launches them. These are an\nacceptance layer for Step 09, not protocol-specific code inside the Agent\nCoordination kernel.\n\nStep 09 considers read-only/mutation as an execution-effect dimension, but its\nMVP uses only read-only/session-local artifact production. Work, git, repo\nmutation, merge, and lifecycle transitions remain Step 10 or later concerns."
  },
